body.p: Upon entry, claims 1-3, 5-6, 8-10, 12-13 and 15-22 are pending in this application, of which claims 1 and 8 are independent. By this response, claims 1-3, 5-6, 8-10, and 12-13 are amended, and claims 4, 7, 11, and 14 have been cancelled without prejudice or disclaimer. New claims 15- 22 have been added. All amendments made to the claims are fully supported by the specification as originally filed, for example, by Fig. 2B, paragraphs 0045-47 and 0063-0064, and the original claims. Hence, no new matter has been introduced.

The arguments and contentions presented herein should not be construed as any acquiescence or agreement by Applicant with the reasoning stated in the Office Action regardless of whether or not the following remarks specifically address any particular argument or contention from the Office Action. Furthermore, although certain distinctions between the claims of the present application and the cited references are addressed below, these distinctions are not necessarily exhaustive.
Reconsideration of this application for allowance of all pending claims is hereby respectfully requested in view of the amendments to the claims and following remarks.
Applicant believes that these amendments are fully responsive to the Examiner's concerns. Withdrawal of the objection to the disclosure is, therefore, respectfully solicited.
Claims 1 and 8 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(2) as being anticipated by Park (U.S. Publication No. 2022/0332319 A1, hereinafter "Park").

Claims 2-3, 6, 9-10 and 13 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Park as applied to claims 1 and 8 above, and further in view of Grace et al. (U.S. Publication No. 2021/0304607 Al, hereinafter "Grace").

Claims 4 and 11 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Park in view of Grace as applied to claims 2 and 9 above, and further in view of Rajab et al. (U.S. Publication No. 2019/0329777 Al, hereinafter "Rajab").

Claims 5 and 12 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Park in view of Grace and Rajab as applied to claims 4 and 11 above, and further in view of Kato et al. (US Publication No. 2020/0247417 Al, hereinafter "Kato").
Claims 7 and 14 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Park as applied to claims 1 and 8 above, and further in view of Rajab.
These rejections are traversed for the following reasons.
Without acquiescing to the merits of these rejections, and solely in the interest of expediting prosecution, independent claim 1 is amended to incorporate subject matter from dependent claim
4 and additional features, as shown below (emphasis added):
the processor detects the change in the position of the preceding vehicle
and predicts occurrence of the preset event using an event prediction model based
on the detected change in the position of the preceding vehicle, and
the event prediction model is trained based on information related to the
detected change in the position of the preceding vehicle using a machine learning

In the rejection of claim 4 (subject matter of which has been incorporated into claim 1), the Examiner admits that Park and Grace do not teach "the processor detects the change in the position of the preceding vehicle and predicts the preset event using a preset model based on the change in the position of the preceding vehicle" of the claim, but relies on Rajab as allegedly making up for the admitted deficiencies of Park and Grace. It is respectfully submitted that Rajab does not teach or suggest the amended recitations of claim 1.

Rajab's prediction model is merely "a lookup table based on naturalistic behavior data" (claim 7) on relationships between "the velocity differential between the following vehicle 208 and the first preceding vehicle 210" and "the spacing between the following vehicle 208 and the first preceding vehicle 210" (see paragraphs 0062-0063) for "identifying a potential lane change location and receiving proximate vehicle data associated with proximate vehicles" (underline added, see paragraph 0005). Rajab discloses "[t]he prediction plots 400 and 410-460 are illustrative of the data binning and data fit estimation being used to predict a kinematic data at

predictive increments, however, the data may be used as a look-up table or other accessible data form" (see paragraph 0062). That is, as illustrated in Fig. 2 of Rajab (reproduced below with annotation), Rajab's model is a prediction model of a potential lane change or cut-in of a proximate vehicle (on lane 202) to a lane (204) on which the following vehicle 208 and the first preceding vehicle 210 are located, rather than "change in the position of the preceding vehicle (to an adjacent lane)" (emphasis added), as recited in claim 1.
SVG {EMBED HERE} 3.540.92 I SVG {EMBED HERE} 3.1431.237 I Fig. 2 of Rajab (left, annotated) and Fig. 2B of the present application (right, annotated)

On the other hand, as illustrated in Fig. 2B of the present application (reproduced above with annotation) showing one exemplary embodiment of the present disclosure, a processor may detect a change in a position of a preceding vehicle 240 and predict occurrence of a preset event (e.g., a sudden lane change of a preceding vehicle due to a vehicle in front of the preceding vehicle having stopped) using an event prediction model based on the detected change in the position of the preceding vehicle 240. Here, the event prediction model may be trained based on information related to the detected change in the position of the preceding vehicle 240 using a machine learning algorithm.

In addition, the data plots in Figs. 4A-4G of Rajab merely show relative velocity data between the following vehicle 208 and the first preceding vehicle 210 and the space therebetween, but do not show position change data of the proximate vehicle 206. Therefore, Rajab also fails to
teach "predicts occurrence of the preset event using an event prediction model based on the detected change in the position of the preceding vehicle" (emphasis added), as recited in claim 1.

Furthermore, Rajab discloses, at best, "the prediction model may be based on simulated data or naturalistic data ... may be based on second-by-second vehicle trajectory data from a Verkehr In Stadten-Simulations model (VISSIM) freeway network" (see paragraph 0060). However, such a simulation software package that Rajab discloses, e.g., VISSIM, does not satisfy "the event prediction model is trained based on information related to the detected change in the position of the preceding vehicle using a machine learning algorithm" (emphasis added), as recited in claim 1.

In view of the foregoing aspects of Rajab, it is respectfully submitted that Rajab does not teach or suggest the aforementioned features of claim 1, and therefore fails to cure the admitted deficiencies of Park and Grace.

Kato, which is cited for allegedly teaching "the point being separated by a distance exceeding 1/3 of a total width of the preceding vehicle from any one lane marking of a corresponding side of the lane in which the preceding vehicle is traveling" of claim 5, does not remedy the aforementioned Park, Grace, and Rajab.

Based on all the foregoing, it is respectfully submitted that the cited references, whether taken alone or in combination, do not disclose, teach or suggest each and every feature in the particular combination embodied by claim 1. "All words in a claim must be considered in judging the patentability of that claim against the prior art." In re Wilson, 165 USPQ 494, 496 (CCPA 1970). Accordingly, claim 1 and the claims dependent thereupon are allowable over the prior art of record.

Independent claim 8 is directed to a method for preventing car collision. While of different scope than claim 1, independent claim 8, as amended, includes recitations substantially similar to those argued above in relation to claim 1. Hence, claim 8 and the claims dependent thereupon are allowable over the cited prior art for at least reasons similar to those discussed above with respect to claim 1.
Applicant therefore submits that the rejections of the claims are overcome and respectfully requests that the rejections of the claims under 35 U.S.C. §§ 102/103 be withdrawn.

Dependent claims 15-22 are added. Support for these claims can be found in, e.g., paragraphs 0046-47 and 0063-0064 of the application-as-filed. No new matter is added. Separate from dependency from claim 1 or claim 8, none of the cited references teaches or suggests subject matter of claims 15-22, and claims 15-22 are allowable over the cited art.

In view of the above amendments and remarks, Applicant submits that this application should be allowed and the case passed to issue. If there are any questions regarding this Amendment or the application in general, a telephone call to the undersigned would be appreciated to expedite the prosecution of the application.
